tasks.prompt: Audit these parcel geometries before overlay. Identify which need repair, but do not silently remove empty records or force every repair into a Polygon.
tasks.inputs: A known-CRS GeoPackage with stable IDs: a self-crossing bow-tie Polygon, a collapsed polygon ring, a null geometry, an empty Polygon, valid Polygon/MultiPolygon records, and a valid Point in a mixed-geometry layer. Include authoritative intended repair regions and attribute nulls.
acceptance: Run python -m terraproof check parcels.gpkg; expected_checks applies to the original seeded input inventory.
Report null, empty and invalid counts separately and distinguish exact geometry types from families.
Show a proposed make_valid repair ledger retaining original IDs, type/dimension changes and collapsed parts; require review before dropping anything.
Do not present a successful validity repair as proof that the intended parcel regions were recovered.
tasks.pitfall: Repair hides collapsed lower-dimensional pieces, nulls or missing scope while producing a valid-looking output.

tasks.prompt: These zoning polygons each validate, but the coverage total looks wrong. Find overlaps, gaps, slivers and duplicate shapes without dissolving away zone identities.
tasks.inputs: A projected polygon GeoPackage with individually valid, nonempty Polygon/MultiPolygon records, an expected coverage boundary, a positive-area overlap, an uncovered strip, an authorized interior hole, a narrow overlay fragment and equal geometries with different ring/vertex ordering and different attributes.
acceptance: Run python -m terraproof check zones.gpkg; expected_checks applies to the individually valid seeded coverage, which should pass these per-feature checks despite coverage defects.
Measure overlap regions and boundary-minus-union gaps in justified units, excluding the documented legitimate hole and shared-edge-only contacts.
Identify topological duplicates independently of WKB ordering; explain any legitimate co-located records rather than deleting them by shape alone.
Report slivers against a fixture-supplied accuracy/tolerance policy and compare topology after any snapping or precision change.
State that coverage topology and duplicate detection are not checked automatically yet.
tasks.pitfall: Per-feature validity is confused with a gap-free, non-overlapping coverage, and exact-byte deduplication misses equivalent shapes.

tasks.prompt: Join owner attributes to parcels and export RFC 7946 GeoJSON without losing unmatched parcels. Diagnose why the supplied legacy join looks complete but contains fewer records.
tasks.inputs: A valid, nonempty projected parcel layer with unique stable IDs; an owner table with a duplicate key, a null key and an unmatched parcel key; a legacy inner-join polygon output with fewer rows; polygons with holes and initially opposite RFC winding. Include expected ID sets and owner relationships.
acceptance: Run python -m terraproof check legacy_join.gpkg --compare-to parcels.gpkg; expected_checks applies to the seeded legacy output, not the corrected export.
Audit attribute nulls, duplicate/null join keys, unmatched records and join cardinality before selecting an explicit owner-resolution policy.
Produce a reviewed left-join result preserving every parcel ID; detect record substitution even when total counts agree.
Export longitude/latitude WGS 84 GeoJSON with counterclockwise exteriors and clockwise holes, then reopen and compare IDs, nulls, types and ring coordinates.
State that scope.record_count does not validate join semantics, attributes or GeoJSON winding.
tasks.pitfall: An inner join or null-key handling silently drops or multiplies parcels, and valid polygons are exported with the wrong coordinate/winding contract.
